name: A Church Divided: The Reformation and Its Wars
description: From Gutenberg's press and Luther's protest to the Thirty Years' War: how a quarrel over the Church broke Christian Europe into rival camps.

checkpoints.name: Ink and unrest
checkpoints.note: Johannes Gutenberg's printing press made books cheaper, and the Gutenberg Bible was among the first big books printed in Europe. New ideas could now travel faster than the Church could answer them.

checkpoints.name: Luther's protest
checkpoints.note: Martin Luther's Ninety-five Theses of 1517 challenged Church practices, and the Reformation spread under Emperor Charles V. Zwingli led reform in Switzerland, Erasmus urged change from within, and the Peasants' War broke out. Calvin began his work, Henry VIII broke with Rome, Thomas More died in 1535, and the Jesuits were founded in 1540.

checkpoints.name: Rulers, queens and fleets
checkpoints.note: Edward VI, Mary I and Elizabeth I each led England's Church in a different direction. In the Dutch Revolt the Netherlands rose against Spain, in 1588 the Spanish Armada failed to invade England, and in 1598 the Edict of Nantes gave French Protestants a measure of toleration.

checkpoints.name: Plots and war
checkpoints.note: The Gunpowder Plot to blow up Parliament failed in 1605. The Thirty Years' War devastated Germany, Gustavus Adolphus led the Swedes into it, and the Peace of Westphalia ended it in 1648, leaving Europe divided between Catholic and Protestant states.
